• Temperament: males are very aggressive and should be kept alone or in tanks with non-male bettas. Can be kept in a planted community tank of multiple females if there is adequate space.
  • Max size: 2.3 inches (about 5.8 cm); another description gives a maximum standard length of about 1.4 inches (3.6 cm).
  • TDS: 60–200 (kept in soft water with low TDS, but tolerant of water conditions).
  • pH: 5.0–7.0
  • Temperature: 75–85°F (24–29°C); much better coloration at warmer temperatures above 78°F (26°C).
  • Diet: carnivorous.
  • Breeding: bubble nester.
  • IUCN Red List: N/A

Native to slow-moving, shallow waters in eastern Thailand (Chachoengsao, Sa Kaeo, Prachin Buri, Chon Buri provinces), western Cambodia, and parts of Vietnam. This listing is wild caught from the type locality of Long An, Vietnam.

Found in freshwater marshes, rice paddies, ponds, and canals with dense vegetation and low oxygen, relying on its labyrinth organ for breathing. They live in still-water marshes and ditches in Southeast Asia. Prefers warm, slightly acidic to neutral water (pH 6.8–7.4).
Both B. imbellis and B. siamorientalis prefer warmer water. Temperature 24–29°C, with better coloration above 26°C; pH 5.0–7.0; TDS 60–200.
Carnivorous. Fed live blackworms, frozen bloodworms and pellets.
Males are very aggressive and should be kept alone or in tanks with non-male bettas. Multiple females can be kept in a planted community tank if there is adequate space.

Males display vivid red patches on the caudal, anal, and pelvic fins, with iridescent blue or green accents. Females are duller, with brownish bodies and muted red or silvery markings. The operculum is black with two parallel reddish vertical bars in males (sometimes pale red, greenish-silvery, or plain silvery in certain populations); females have less distinct, faded opercular markings.

This species closely resembles Betta imbellis but has a darker body and head, which is why it is sometimes called the "black imbellis". It lacks the facial iridescence of B. imbellis, giving a classic black head. Like all wild bettas, its natural coloration is metallic green. Body: slender and elongated, typical of the Betta splendens complex, slightly compressed; maximum standard length about 3.6 cm, one of the smaller species in the group. Caudal fin short and rounded, often with a red crescent-shaped distal band and a thin black edge, less elaborate than Betta splendens. Coloration: dark brown to black body with a higher proportion of black scales compared with iridescent blue/green ones.
